newsitem.title: USA: NTSB to probe incident involving airliner, fighters.
newsitem.headline: NTSB to probe incident involving airliner, fighters.

text.p: The National Transportation Safety Board will investigate this week's incident off the New Jersey coast involving a chartered Boeing 727 airliner and two Air National Guard F-16 fighters, an NTSB official said Friday.

In what the charter's operator described as a near-collision, the passenger jet manoeuvred violently in response to cockpit collision warnings when it was approached by one of the fighter jets Wednesday.
The NTSB official, who asked not to be identified, said the board's investigation would be conducted independently of a probe already being conducted by the Air Force.

The Pentagon, meanwhile, denied that the incident was a "near collision", saying that one of the New Jersey Air National Guard F-16s had carefully approached to 1,000 feet behind and 1,000 feet below the Nations Air Boeing 727, which was en route from San Juan, Puerto Rico, to New York with about 80 passengers.
"I can't call it a near collision," said Air Force Maj. Tom Schultz, a Defence Department spokesman. "The reaction of the civilian (airliner) pilots was in response to their collision warnings."

NBC, which first reported the incident on Thursday, quoted Mark McDonald, president of Smyrna, Georgia-based Nations Air, as saying that the plane was was forced to dive, climb and climb again to avoid a collision. The airliner later landed safely at John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York.
